text: Tourist here from America. The dialysis process went smoothly. I emailed the facility and got a prompt response. I'm on a TTS schedule (3, 4-hour treatments/week). I was usually finished by 6pm and the cost pretty reasonable. I had to pay out of pocket because my insurance from the states will not work there. Each treatment cost approximately $45 USD which is far better than HCM in Vietnam and the philippines. If you can't speak thai there is at least one nurse available for you. The atmosphere is welcoming and cozy and you're not too far from plenty to do in Bangkok. There are plenty of nearby hotels and popular attractions. It also reminds me of a spa. There are other cosmetic and medical services offered in the same medical facility on different floors as well. Payment is accepted after each treatment and since Bangkok never sleeps you'll never miss out on anything. The only major difference I noticed between this facility and the facility I used in the states is that the use of saline (salt) it's used more conservatively in Thailand so bring mustard or salt tablets if you're the type who cramps. Also, bring your medications as well some meds are not carried here so check first.

text:
This is absolutely terrible. I can confirm again that the staff and doctors are awful. They wrote down the patient's temperature without actually measuring it. I had a rapid heartbeat and shortness of breath, but the doctor was indifferent, didn't examine me, and ignored my symptoms. They just prescribed paracetamol and allergy medication.

Two weeks passed, and I went back for a second visit with the same symptoms. It was Friday morning, and they said there was no doctor available and I should come back on Monday. The staff verbally told me to go to the emergency room at the hospital, but the hospital refused. When I asked for a referral letter, they couldn't provide one because there was no doctor available and they didn't have any medical records from the previous visit where the doctor didn't examine me at all.

When I called the National Health Security Office (NHSO) at 1330, another doctor came down within three minutes (why did they hide earlier? I don't understand). When I explained the rapid heartbeat and shortness of breath, the doctor said it was because I wanted a referral letter that my heart was beating fast. Are they crazy? It's been two weeks, and they said they wouldn't know because the doctor didn't use any equipment to examine me. This doctor said, ***"You have to understand, if this were a private hospital, the doctor would examine you completely. But because of the NHSO health insurance, it's preventing me from doing so."*** If you talk like that, you shouldn't be a doctor.

If I hadn't called and complained to the National Health Security Office (NHSO), they wouldn't have bothered to come see me. It was a complete waste of time and money on transportation. I'm telling everyone, run away! Don't come here. You only have a gold card (universal health coverage), they won't treat you.
The doctor and staff here are very kind and helpful. This is my second visit. At first, I didn't see the parking area; there's clinic parking in the alley next to the Heia Chai noodle shop.

This is the worst 30-baht health clinic I've ever been to. It's incredibly complicated and inconsiderate of patients' travel difficulties. I'm an elderly person who can't walk well, and I personally don't want elderly people to walk too much because they might fall. They should only walk when absolutely necessary, like when going to the hospital. They said that if you're not bedridden, you have to come to the clinic; if you can go to the hospital, you should be able to come to the clinic too. The staff are constantly rude to patients, and I've seen it happen many times. The wait times are ridiculously long. If they're not willing to treat patients and the service is terrible, the rules and regulations are more numerous than in high school. How many times does one person have to go to the hospital just to get a referral slip? Waiting for half a day is insane! Has the clinic ever discussed or clarified this with the hospital? The referral slip issue is a huge problem. The service used to be much better; the staff were good, and the rules weren't unfair to patients. I spend so much money on transportation to the hospital every day.
And getting medication takes forever.
This clinic is not suitable for the elderly or those with mobility limitations. Thank you.

The service was terrible. I called to inquire about information and the employee hung up on me.

text: Poor service, discrimination, gossiping about other patients to people who don't know anything. Every time I see a doctor, in less than a minute, they prescribe paracetamol.

We'll have to do everything ourselves, measure and record blood pressure, and walk around in a flurry. They won't explain how to use the equipment. They're not a Buddhist, so they don't know what to do. The worst part is the doctor. If all they can say is that they suspect pneumonia, then why not be a doctor? They'll just take their medicine first. If that's all you're going to do, you might as well go to the pharmacy.

The operator had very bad words. I have COVID but have gold card rights here. The nurse told me to print the photos, which is not convenient for me. Not everyone who has COVID has a printer at home. So I asked if there is another option. The nurse replied that I should buy my own medicine and pay for it myself. I just want to know the reason. Is there another option that can make it more convenient for me? What do you use the printed photos for? But your answer is too bad. If you give a good reason, I would be happy to find a way to print them for you. But you tell me to pay for my own medicine. Seriously, where is your ethics? Not everyone will be able to print documents for you. And what if it's an elderly person? Don't they have to lie around and wait until their symptoms become severe?
